messages:
marta: Heads up — after the kernel-selector change yesterday we observed a sharp rise in GPU-side OOMs tied to KV cache fragmentation. attaching quick tl;dr of what i saw in the traces.

sam: ugh. repro steps?

yuji: saw this too in perf dashboard —  p50s fine but p99 spikes & OOM coincident with kernel change that favors fused-matmul kernel for short sequences.

marta: repro: small local cluster with mixed model variants. when selector picks fused-matmul path, slot allocation becomes more granular, which increases fragmentation of GPU cache slabs. result: effective free bytes drop even though nominal usage same.

aditya: can you paste the eviction snapshot from timeline?

marta: pasted snippet below (from heapdump + ttl sweep logs):
```
EVICT_TRACE: step=120 current_gpu_free_mb=512 slab_frag_ratio=0.42 evicted_slots=136 ttl_sweeps=3 kernel_path=fused-matmul
KV_STATS: total_slots=8192 hotset_ratio=0.22 avg_key_len=48 key_entropy=0.87
```

pri: @marta does this correlate with the canonicalizer change last week? we changed prefix hashing to use murmur3 v2 which may change bucket distribution.

marta: probably orthogonal but could amplify. murmur3 shift increased collisions for short prompts by ~3% which increases bucket chaining — more small allocations. combined with fused kernel slab split we end up with many tiny free fragments.

sam: idea: add a soft-upper-bound for GPU cache that triggers proactive compaction before OOM instead of waiting for TTL sweep. simple heuristic: if frag_ratio > 0.35 && free_mb < 1.2 * avg_token_batch_mb then trigger compaction.

aditya: ^ I like that. compaction is expensive, need to ensure it runs off the hot request path. infra-bot can schedule a background compaction job per node.

infra-bot: scheduled compaction job node=ai-gpu-07 start_t=3185007600 expected_dur_s=12 reason=frag_ratio_trigger

yuji: also, on kernel selector side we can bias away from fused-matmul for sequences < 64 to avoid slab re-splitting. tolerable latency uplift but reduces fragmentation.

pri: for tuning TTL: current defaults are 600s on GPU cache and 1200s on CPU. maybe reduce GPU TTL to 180s for high-frag workloads, and increase CPU to act as overflow.

marta: config snippet i tested locally:
```json
{
  "kv_cache": {
    "gpu_capacity_mb": 12288,
    "cpu_capacity_mb": 24576,
    "gpu_ttl_seconds": 180,
    "cpu_ttl_seconds": 1800,
    "evict_policy": "adaptive-seg-lru",
    "compaction_threshold": 0.35
  }
}
```

aditya: results?

marta: in synthetic replay for the hotset, 99th compaction runs prevented 3 OOMs across 1000s of requests, p99 latency increased by ~18ms during compaction windows but overall error rate dropped. hit-rate on short prefixes dropped ~1.4% (they got demoted to CPU) but end-to-end tail latency improved because OOMs vanished.

sam: we should add a small metric panel: gpu_frag_ratio, compaction_count, post_compaction_free_mb, cpu_absorb_rate. also alert when compaction_count > 5 per hour.

yuji: agreed. will add to perf dashboard and create a canary config rollout to 10% of nodes.

pri: also add a sampling profiler to capture kernel-switch decisions + cache key sizes when compaction triggers to help root cause.

marta: next steps: (1) canary kernel selector change that biases against fused path for seq<64 (2) implement background compaction with config flags (3) short GPU TTL/CPU overflow experiment (4) dashboard + alerts.

aditya: schedule sync with runtime owners tomorrow 10:30 to approve canary.

sam: thanks — tagging this for postmortem notes if we see recurrence. :thumbsup:

marta: adding raw traces to the shared drive and a short runbook for on-call to proactively trigger compaction if frag_ratio > 0.45 and free_mb < 400.

infra-bot: uploaded artifacts to s3://redwood-perf/artifacts/3185004321-frag-run/

marta: will follow up with a small PR for the selector and compaction toggle.

pri: cool — keep the notes concise in the PR description so SRE can audit the compaction behavior.

marta: will do. thanks everyone.
